files.note: REQ trace cites 313-410; actual copyFile+moveFile+deleteFile span 313-421 (deleteFile runs to 421, not 410). All three are synchronous single-shot async methods today -- no state machine, no awaiting-decision concept, no cancellation hook. This is the addition site to wrap in a job/state-machine service.

files.note: Delete has the same shape: one fire-and-forget call, no per-item progress. AC-4 (progress by processed item count, not bytes) needs a manual directory walk instead of fs.rm(recursive).

files.note: Already implemented and unit-tested (FR-FOP-004 AC-1/AC-2 marked checked:true in the REQ). files.signature: try { await fs.rename(srcResolved, destResolved); } catch (err) { if (code === 'EXDEV') { await this.copyFile(...); await this.deleteFile(...); return; } ... }
files.note: REQ trace ':377-390' matches exactly; the EXDEV branch itself is lines 381-384 (matches AC-6's 'moveFile:381-384' citation exactly: if EXDEV -> copyFile -> deleteFile -> return). AC-6 is correct that this branch has no partial/cancellable intermediate state today: copyFile and deleteFile are each awaited to completion as opaque units, so a cancel during EXDEV move can only land on 'both survive' or 'both gone', not 'partial file' as AC-1/AC-2 require. AC-5 (fs.rename is atomic, no mid-state, late cancel must be a no-op not a failure) is true of the fs.rename branch (378) as-is.

files.signature: export type ServerWsMessage = | ScreenSnapshotMessage | ... | { type: 'connected'; clientId: string } | { type: 'pong' };
files.note: The full outbound union. Addition site for file-job:progress / file-job:decision-required / file-job:done as three new arm(s), most naturally as inline object types following the same '| { type: ...; sessionId: string; ... }' idiom used for cwd/status/session:error (lines 803-805).

files.signature: broadcastWs(sessionId: string, event: string, payload: object): void { this.wsRouter?.sendSessionEvent(sessionId, event, payload); }
files.note: THE existing per-session WS push API, already used in production for 'status' (1944), 'cwd' (4965), 'session:exited' (6733). This is the call a file-job service should use: sessionManager.broadcastWs(sessionId, 'file-job:progress', {...}) produces the wire message {type:'file-job:progress', sessionId, ...payload}. Caveat: it is keyed by exactly ONE sessionId, but IR-FOP-001 AC-2 lets sourceSessionId and destSessionId differ -- if a client is only subscribed to the destination session's panel it will not receive pushes unless the job service calls broadcastWs twice (once per distinct session) or a session-pair variant is added.

files.note: sendSessionEvent iterates this.sessionSubscribers.get(sessionId) and calls sendTo(ws, {type:event, sessionId, ...payload}) for each socket (line 5997). sendTo itself is at 7279-7328 and does the actual transport-queue/backpressure-aware send.

A separate, unrelated push API that sends to literally every connected client regardless of session subscription. Not the right primitive for file-job pushes (would leak job progress to clients not viewing that session) -- included here only so it isn't confused with sendSessionEvent.

ws_push_api: sessionManager.broadcastWs(sessionId: string, event: string, payload: object): void (server/src/services/SessionManager.ts:7034-7037) is the established, already-in-production per-session push API (used today for 'status', 'cwd', 'session:exited'). It delegates to WsRouter.sendSessionEvent(sessionId, event, payload) (ws/WsRouter.ts:5985-5999), which looks up this.sessionSubscribers.get(sessionId) and calls sendTo(ws, {type: event, sessionId, ...payload}) (sendTo itself: 7279-7328) for every subscribed socket. It is keyed by exactly one sessionId; there is a separate, unrelated broadcastAll(event, data, excludeClientId?) (7101-7107) that sends to every connected client regardless of subscription and is NOT appropriate for job pushes. Because IR-FOP-001 AC-2 allows sourceSessionId != destSessionId, a job that wants both panels updated must call broadcastWs once per distinct session id (no built-in multi-session fan-out exists).

session_lifecycle: Sessions live in SessionManager's private `sessions: Map<string, SessionData>` (services/SessionManager.ts:1191). Created by `createSession(...)` (1329). Deleted via either `deleteSession(id, reason)` (3250-3259, synchronous, used for the direct-delete path) or `terminateSession(id, options)` (3262-3313, async, does process-tree termination first) -- both funnel into private `finalizeSession(sessionId, data, options)` (6701-...) which marks `data.finalized = true`, clears timers, records cleanup observation, optionally calls `broadcastWs(sessionId, 'session:exited', ...)` (line 6733 inside finalizeSession) and kills the pty. The HTTP layer (`routes/sessionRoutes.ts`, DELETE /:id at 61-83) wraps this with two injectable lifecycle hooks declared in `SessionRoutesOptions` (7-9): `onSessionDeleting` (called at line 69, before `terminateSession`) and `onSessionDeleted` (called at line 72, only after successful termination). `index.ts:904-906` wires only `onSessionDeleting` today (to `workspaceService.markSessionStoppedByDirectDelete`); `onSessionDeleted` is declared but currently unused anywhere in index.ts, making it the natural, already-existing hook for a file-job registry to cancel/purge jobs keyed to a deleted session without modifying SessionManager or sessionRoutes.ts themselves.
